title: Acne scars & keloids
summary: Atrophic (ice-pick, boxcar, rolling) vs raised (hypertrophic, keloid) scars, scar vs pigment, and which specialist modalities suit which scar. Prevention is treating active acne early.

glance.think: Depressions or raised scars after inflammatory acne. Patients often call flat pigment ‘scarring’ too.
glance.engine: Inflammatory destruction of collagen (atrophic), or excess aberrant collagen (hypertrophic, or keloid beyond the original borders).
glance.backbone: Control active acne first, then refer to specialist modalities matched to scar type, with realistic expectations.
glance.never_miss: Scarring at any acne severity is an NG198 referral trigger. Also look for psychological distress and keloid tendency before procedures.

what.title: Scope: counselling and recognition
what.text: For the pharmacist/IP, this page covers recognising types, setting expectations, safety and referral. It is **not** a procedure how-to (no injection technique, laser settings or peel recipes).

what: Acne scarring is fibrous remodelling after inflammatory acne. **Atrophic** scars follow collagen destruction. **Hypertrophic or keloid** scars follow excess collagen. Scars are usually permanent but may soften with time or combined treatment. The psychological impact is often high, even when the scarring looks ‘mild’.

list: Inflammatory nodules and cysts cause net **collagen destruction**, giving **atrophic** scars (ice-pick, boxcar, rolling).
Excess collagen gives **hypertrophic** scars (within the original lesion) or **keloids** (spreading **beyond** the original borders).
Risk rises with acne severity and duration, picking (acne excoriée) and smoking. Keloids and PIH are more common in **skin of colour**.
**Post-inflammatory erythema and hyper- or hypopigmentation** are colour change, not true scarring, but patients often call both ‘scars’.

head: Type
Appearance
Typical sites
rows: Narrow, deep, V-shaped; deeper than wide (about 60–70% of atrophic scars)
Round or oval depressions with sharp vertical edges
Wider, sloping edges, tethered by dermal bands
Raised, same size as the original lesion
Firm raised scar **beyond** the original borders; may itch or hurt

diagnosis: Clinical: history of acne plus scar morphology. Document **Fitzpatrick skin type**, whether acne is still active, and the patient’s goals. Biopsy is rarely needed, only for an atypical, evolving ‘keloid’.

head: Look-alike
Distinguishing clues
rows: Flat colour change, with no depression or elevation
Dermatofibroma or tumour mimicking a keloid
Solitary, atypical nodule. Refer if in doubt

management: Treat active acne **early and adequately** (see [Acne vulgaris](condition:acne-vulgaris)). **Scarring is a referral trigger** under NICE NG198. Treat active acne first, before any scar procedures.

head: Scar type
Options (specialist or cosmetic)
rows: **TCA CROSS** (chemical reconstruction of skin scars), punch excision or grafting
Resurfacing (fractional lasers, peels), punch techniques, microneedling
**Subcision**, dermal fillers or fat, microneedling, fractional laser
**Silicone** gel or sheet, potent topical steroid under occlusion, **intralesional steroid** (specialist), pulsed dye laser, cryotherapy, careful revision (**high recurrence**)

management: Combined, multi-session approaches are usual. Refer to dermatology, plastic surgery or a reputable aesthetic clinic, and explain that the aim is **improvement, not removal**.
red_flags: Scarring or significant distress at any acne severity: refer (NG198).
Low mood, anxiety or body dysmorphic concerns: signpost or refer for mental health support.
A rapidly growing or atypical ‘keloid’: exclude a tumour.
Keloid tendency or skin of colour before elective procedures: use an experienced operator only.
pearls: **Separate scar from pigment.** The treatments are different.
Skin of colour carries a higher risk of PIH and keloid after procedures.
OTC silicone gel is a reasonable first step for early raised scars. Use it for months, not weeks.
Check isotretinoin status before procedures: see [Cosmetic procedures](condition:cosmetic-procedures).
